sections.heading: Accessibility as Vibe
sections.body: An inclusive product feels better for everyone. We set color contrast, keyboard navigation, and readable copy as vibe criteria, not compliance checkboxes. Accessibility makes interactions more predictable and reduces cognitive load.

sections.heading: Focus Management
sections.body: We never trap focus. We provide visible indicators and reasonable tab order. Dialogs restore focus to the originating control when dismissed. Keyboard shortcuts are documented and discoverable.

sections.heading: Motion Sensitivity
sections.body: We respect reduced motion preferences and avoid essential meaning encoded only in motion. We use opacity changes or scale adjustments as subtle alternatives. Users can turn off celebratory effects.

sections.heading: Copy and Reading Level
sections.body: We aim for simple sentences, active voice, and consistent terminology. We avoid insider jargon and provide plain-language summaries for complex actions. Tooltips help but should not carry essential meaning alone.

sections.heading: Exercises
sections.body: Audit a screen for keyboard-only use. Increase contrast for the most important call to action. Test with screen reader basics and rewrite any unclear labels.
